lead: A `?string` does not narrow into a `string` return position, and the fix is `as` rather than a different `if`.
body: `if ($v == null) { return "<none>"; } return $v;` is `E0403: this method declares `string` but returns `string|null``, and inverting the test reports the same one line up. Write `return $v as string;` after the null test; the same `as` re-supplies the type inside an expression (`Core\Str::slice($s, ($at as uint) as int)`).
